editorial:
Ever wondered why a simple plant caused so much chaos and fear for decades? You get a front-row seat to that madness in this eye-opening documentary. Narrated by the laid-back Woody Harrelson, the film feels less like a boring history lesson and more like a chat with a friend who has all the inside scoops. It uses a great mix of old clips and funny commentary to show how the US government spent years trying to scare people away from weed, even when the science didn't back it up. The vibe is lighthearted but makes you think about how weird laws can be.

What really makes this work is the pacing; it never feels slow because the footage is so bizarre and entertaining. You will love how it breaks down the propaganda used in the past. While some of the old video quality is a bit grainy, it actually adds to the retro charm of the story. If you are into social history or just want a chill watch, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing that despite all the scary stories and strict laws, marijuana never really went away. It ends by highlighting the gap between the government's fear-mongering and the reality of how people actually use the drug. The final scenes leave you with the idea that the war on weed was more about control and politics than actual health risks, ending on a hopeful note about truth and common sense.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves learning about weird history and social issues.
